farraa:1-1.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَبِّحِ ٱسْمَ رَبِّكَ﴾, and ﴿باسم ربك﴾.
Both of these have occurred, and it is of the speech of the Arabs.

farraa:3-3.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَٱلَّذِي قَدَّرَ فَهَدَىٰ﴾.
He determined His creation, and guided the male of the beasts to the way of approaching the female.
It is also said: He determined and guided and led astray; so mention of guidance sufficed for mention of misguidance, because of how often it accompanies it. The readers are agreed on the doubled form (قدّر). Abū ʿAbd al-Raḥmān al-Sulamī used to read قَدَر, lightened, and they consider it to be from the reading of ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may Allah have mercy on him) [135/a]. The doubled form is dearer to me because the readers agree on it.

farraa:5-7.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَجَعَلَهُ غُثَآءً أَحْوَىٰ﴾.
When vegetation becomes dry, it is غثاء (stubble). الأحوى: what has turned black from age. It may also be: He brought forth the pasture dark green (أحوى), then made it stubble; so it is placed later while its meaning is earlier.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿سَنُقْرِئُكَ فَلاَ تَنسَىٰ إِلاَّ مَا شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ﴾.
He did not will that he should forget anything. It is like His saying: ﴿خَالِدِينَ فِيهَا مَا دَامَتِ السَّماوَاتُ والأَرْضُ إِلاَّ مَا شَاءَ رَبُّك﴾, and He does not will [otherwise]. You would say in speech: "I will surely give you all that you ask, except what I will" and "unless I will to deny you", while the intention is not to deny him. On this pattern run the oaths in which an exception is made, while the swearer's intention is fulfilment.

farraa:11-11.t:
His saying, Blessed and Exalted is He: ﴿وَيَتَجَنَّبُهَا ٱلأَشْقَى﴾.
He avoids the reminder and does not take heed.

farraa:12-12.t:
His saying, Majestic and Mighty is He: ﴿ٱلنَّارَ ٱلْكُبْرَىٰ﴾.
It is the lowest of the layers of the Fire.

farraa:14-14.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿قَدْ أَفْلَحَ مَن تَزَكَّىٰ﴾.
He did good and gave charity. It is also said: قد أفلح من تزكى: he gave charity before going out on the day of the Eid.

farraa:15-15.t:
﴿وَذَكَرَ ٱسْمَ رَبِّهِ فَصَلَّىٰ﴾.
He attended the prayer with the imam.

farraa:16-16.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَاةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا﴾.
The readers agreed on the tāʾ. In the reading of Ubayy it is: "بَلْ أَنْتُمْ تُؤْثِرُونَ الْحَياةَ", a confirmation for whoever [«لم» in the source, read «لمن»] read with tāʾ.
Some readers read: "بَلْ يُؤْثِرُونَ".

farraa:18-18.t:
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿إِنَّ هَـٰذَا لَفِي ٱلصُّحُفِ ٱلأُولَىٰ﴾.
He says: whoever mentions the name of his Lord and prays and does good — that is in the former scriptures just as it is in the Qurʾān.
